terms.definition: The strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
terms.examiner: "Electrostatic attraction" and "oppositely charged ions" are the marks.

terms.definition: The strong electrostatic attraction between two nuclei and the shared pair of electrons between them.
terms.examiner: Writing only "a shared pair of electrons" may not be enough when the question asks for the attraction.

terms.definition: A covalent bond in which both electrons of the shared pair come from one atom.
terms.examiner: Shown by an arrow from the atom that donates the lone pair.

terms.definition: The strong electrostatic attraction between metal ions and the delocalised electrons.
terms.examiner: Refer to delocalised electrons, not "free" electrons.

terms.definition: The ability of an atom to attract the bonding electrons in a covalent bond.
terms.examiner: Pauling values are in the Data Booklet. A difference in electronegativity between two bonded atoms gives a polar bond.

terms.definition: Instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces: a temporary dipole in one molecule induces a dipole in a neighbouring molecule.
terms.examiner: Present between all molecules; stronger with more electrons and more points of contact between molecules.

terms.definition: The attraction between a δ+ hydrogen bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on N, O or F in another molecule.
terms.examiner: Diagrams need the partial charges, the lone pair and a bond angle of 180° around the hydrogen.

terms.definition: Pairs of electrons around a central atom repel each other and get as far apart as possible; lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs.
terms.examiner: State the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs before naming the shape and the bond angle.
